newsitem.title: BRAZIL: Brazil's police return to work after bloody strike.
newsitem.headline: Brazil's police return to work after bloody strike.

text.p: Brazilian police returned to work in much of the country on Monday as a violent strike over pay drew to a close, the deputy president of the Association of Police Officers said.
"The situation is back to normal in much of the country," Jose Luis de Lira said. But police remained "on alert" to make sure state governments met their promises of higher pay, he added.
One police officer died and at least three others were injured in violent clashes linked to the protests which affected 12 of Brazil's 27 states in June and July.
An army soldier was also shot and killed by armed robbers last week while on patrol in Recife, capital of northeastern Pernambuco state, where police were on strike.
Police in Pernambuco, who went on strike nearly two weeks ago, voted to go back to work on Sunday after winning a proposed pay hike that ranged between 13 percent and 45 percent, de Lira said.

In neighbouring Alagoas state, where army troops were also called out to maintain law and order, police were awaiting confirmation of their proposed salary increases before returning to work, de Lira said.
